issues.description: The solution's animal classes (Seal, Pig, Goat via Animal) define constructors that require both name and age (e.g., Animal(String name, int age)), while the problem statement and the template's Main show/expect single-argument constructors that take only the name (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). This mismatch makes the solution incompatible with the example usage in the template and with the UML/specified attributes, and would confuse students about the required constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent with the problem statement and template. Either (A) update the solution classes to provide single-argument constructors that accept only the name (and optionally overload to add a (name, age) constructor), or (B) update the problem statement and template examples to require and demonstrate two-parameter constructors (name, age). Preferred fix: add single-argument constructors matching the UML/example (e.g., public Animal(String name) and corresponding subclass constructors) so students can use the provided Main examples.

issues.description: The solution's Animal class introduces an 'age' attribute (private int age) which is not present in the UML or described in the problem statement (which states Animal has a name). This structural difference introduces an extra required attribute not documented in the exercise, potentially confusing students about which attributes they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification by removing the extra 'age' attribute from Animal (and its getters/setters) if age is not required by the exercise. Alternatively, if age is intended to be part of the design, update the problem statement, UML diagram, and the template's example usage to explicitly include and document the age attribute so students know to initialize it.

issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal and its subclasses: the problem statement and the template's Main example show/expect single-argument constructors (name only) for Seal, Pig, and Goat, while the solution implementation defines constructors with two parameters (String name, int age) and adds an 'age' attribute to Animal. This difference in constructor signatures and the additional 'age' attribute creates a mapping/confusion for students following the problem text and template example.
issues.suggestedFix: Align constructor signatures across artifacts. Either (A) update the solution to use single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal(String name), Pig(String name), Goat(String name)) and remove the extra 'age' attribute from Animal, or (B) update the problem statement and template/Main example to document and use two-argument constructors (String name, int age) and explicitly mention the new 'age' attribute so students expect the additional parameter.
